explanations.macro_behavior_explanation: At 20°C, control concrete shows temperature-driven microstructural and chemical evolution. Free water removal and early C-S-H dehydroxylation initiate shrinkage; SEM shows incipient microcracks, XRD largely unchanged except slight CH broadening, TGA step near 100°C dominates.

At 200°C, control concrete shows temperature-driven microstructural and chemical evolution. Free water removal and early C-S-H dehydroxylation initiate shrinkage; SEM shows incipient microcracks, XRD largely unchanged except slight CH broadening, TGA step near 100°C dominates.

At 400°C, control concrete shows temperature-driven microstructural and chemical evolution. Pronounced C-S-H dehydration reduces cohesive strength; CH still present but diminishing; SEM reveals wider microcracks; TGA shows bound water loss plateauing; DTA endotherm near 450°C emerges.

At 600°C, control concrete shows temperature-driven microstructural and chemical evolution. CH dehydroxylation largely complete (XRD CH peaks collapse); carbonation phases partially destabilize; micro-CT shows connected crack network.

At 800°C, control concrete shows temperature-driven microstructural and chemical evolution. Decarbonation of CaCO₃ and reconstitution of high-temp calcium silicates reduce matrix integrity; pervasive cracking and high porosity dominate transport and strength.

At 20°C, rubber concrete shows temperature-driven microstructural and chemical evolution. Free water removal and early C-S-H dehydroxylation initiate shrinkage; SEM shows incipient microcracks, XRD largely unchanged except slight CH broadening, TGA step near 100°C dominates. Rubber softening begins (~150–200°C), creating compliant ITZs that concentrate strain but delay continuous cracking; micro-CT shows modest porosity increase localized around rubber.

At 200°C, rubber concrete shows temperature-driven microstructural and chemical evolution. Free water removal and early C-S-H dehydroxylation initiate shrinkage; SEM shows incipient microcracks, XRD largely unchanged except slight CH broadening, TGA step near 100°C dominates. Rubber softening begins (~150–200°C), creating compliant ITZs that concentrate strain but delay continuous cracking; micro-CT shows modest porosity increase localized around rubber.

At 400°C, rubber concrete shows temperature-driven microstructural and chemical evolution. Pronounced C-S-H dehydration reduces cohesive strength; CH still present but diminishing; SEM reveals wider microcracks; TGA shows bound water loss plateauing; DTA endotherm near 450°C emerges. Rubber pyrolysis produces voids/char, amplifying porosity and ITZ degradation; macro stiffness and strength drop faster than control due to void coalescence.

At 600°C, rubber concrete shows temperature-driven microstructural and chemical evolution. CH dehydroxylation largely complete (XRD CH peaks collapse); carbonation phases partially destabilize; micro-CT shows connected crack network. Rubber-derived voids act as crack nucleation sites; crack connectivity and anisotropy increase, explaining accelerated residual strength loss.

At 800°C, rubber concrete shows temperature-driven microstructural and chemical evolution. Decarbonation of CaCO₃ and reconstitution of high-temp calcium silicates reduce matrix integrity; pervasive cracking and high porosity dominate transport and strength. Rubberized mixes exhibit the highest porosity and crack volume; SEM shows collapsed ITZs and large voids where rubber melted away, consistent with severe stiffness/strength degradation.
